games.pitch: Read the grid. Trust your Captain. Don't hit the mine.

howToTitle.heading: How to Play ⚓
howToTitle.subtitle: How to run a successful deployment.

howToStepsRaw: A 5×5 grid of 25 words is dealt face-down. Words belong to one of four roles:
(9 for the first team, 8 for the second),
. Only the Captain can see the roles.
The Captain gives a Sonar Ping.
The Captain sees the colour-coded grid and gives the Crew a Sonar Ping — one word + one number. The word hints at multiple targets. The number says how many payloads it covers.
Using the Sonar Ping, the Crew taps grid words in the order they want to reveal them, then launches the sequence. You can guess up to the Captain's number + 1, or stop early.
Whether hazards end your turn is controlled in Settings.
The game ends when a team arms all of their payloads. The team with the highest Valour wins — not necessarily the team that finished first.
The grid drifts between deployments, scrambling unrevealed cells. Teams can also plant a Jammer tile to ambush the enemy's next sequence.

steps: The Captain gives a Sonar Ping.

games.pitch: The flawless one wins. Don't get exposed.

howToTitle.heading: How to Play 💎
howToTitle.subtitle: Hold the most flawless stone when the vault locks.

howToStepsRaw: Draw one gem so you're holding two, then place one face-up and resolve its effect — keep the other as your secret Showpiece
Effects let you peek, compare, swap, or expose. Get Exposed — a correct guess, a lost appraisal, or being forced to discard the Pink Diamond — and you're out for this Showing.
When the Vault runs dry it's Vault Lock — every Collector still in reveals, highest carat wins. Or simply be the last one standing.

games.pitch: Think alike. And say the same.

howToTitle.heading: How to Play 🧠
howToTitle.subtitle: Find the same connecting word as your partner.

howToStepsRaw: You're each shown the same pair of words. Your job: think of one word that connects them both — without talking to each other.
No peeking! Each player enters their word without showing the other. You also can't use any part of either starting word.
Reveal and check for a match.
After the countdown, both answers are revealed. If they match — Mind Meld! 🧠 If not, your two words become the new starting pair. Keep going until you meld!
The game ends when you achieve Neural Link — both words match. The fewer rounds it took, the stronger the connection. Lower rounds = bigger brains. 🧠
Each round, a random consonant is banned — no clue may contain it. Set your intensity in Settings: Mental Fog for a sub-atomic challenge, or Neural Storm for full supernova mayhem.

steps: Reveal and check for a match.

games.pitch: We've all got issues. Now draw them.

howToTitle.heading: How to Play 🛋️
howToTitle.subtitle: A drawing game about your issues.

howToStepsRaw: Each player is secretly assigned a few Disorders and has to draw them — simultaneously, on their own device. A tip is shown before each drawing to help.
opens a queue of anonymous drawings. For each one, pick the correct disorder from the
. You never see your own drawings.
After time runs out, all drawings are revealed one at a time — with who drew them and who guessed correctly.
Patient +2 — each time a Shrink correctly diagnoses your drawing.
Shrink +2 — for each correct diagnosis you submit.
Speed +1 — the fastest correct diagnosis per drawing.
Tier 3 +1 — bonus for correctly diagnosing a Complex Condition.
The canvas trembles while you draw. Drawings blur into focus during the Shrink Phase — a 3.5 second reveal that tests your eye.

games.pitch: Explain it simply. But no no-nos for me!

howToTitle.heading: How to Play 💬
howToTitle.subtitle: Describe the word without saying anything on the No-No List.

howToStepsRaw: One person describes the Word on screen while their team guesses. Get as many right as you can before the timer runs out!
You also can't say any part of the main word. Use your hands, sounds, or wild metaphors — just no cheating, yeah?
✅ Correct — your team got it, ripper!
⏩ Skip — too hard? Pass it on.
✨ Sylly words — tricky ones worth double points.
Extra Credit words are shuffled into the deck. Correct answers score double, but they carry penalties too — and show all 10 No-No words.

howToStepsRaw: One player is the Friend of a Friend — they don't know the location and are trying to blend in. Everyone else is The Gang — they see a shortlist of possible locations that narrows each plan.
Players message each other over 4 Plans.
Each lap, every player messages one other player. The Gang's shortlist narrows:
. By Plan 3, The Gang knows the exact spot — but the Friend of a Friend might too if they've been paying attention.
Use the map to track locations.
Open 🗺️ any time. The Gang see their narrowing highlights. Friend of a Friend sees all locations and can annotate ✅ Safe or ❌ Dead End.
After the final plan, everyone votes on who they think is the
, and the Friend of a Friend pins their guess on the map.
📍 Friend of a Friend pins correctly → +10 pts.
🕵️ The Gang keeps the secret → +5 each.
🃏 Troublemaker plants a fake → +20 if the Friend of a Friend pins it.

One member of The Gang secretly knows the real location and holds 2 decoy locations. They want the Friend of a Friend to pin a decoy instead. Three-way scoring: Friend of a Friend, The Gang, and The Troublemaker each have different win conditions.

howToTitle.heading: How to Play 🦁
howToTitle.subtitle: Natural Selection — a wildlife documentary goes wrong.

howToStepsRaw: Each habitat draws a new Specimen. Roles are secretly assigned and revealed one at a time:
— each sees a different detail word about the animal.
— only knows the broad grouping (e.g. "Sea Creature"). Trying to blend in.

Over several Observation Days, each player submits one word to describe the Specimen. Turn order is random each day. You can't use the animal's name, and you can't repeat a word already given this habitat.
Once all days are done, the field notes are revealed. Each player votes for who they think is The Mole. Most votes = exposed.
If The Mole is caught, they get one final chance — name the Specimen. The Lead Biologist decides if it counts. +10 Credibility either way for a correct guess.

howToTitle.heading: How to Play 🐑
howToTitle.subtitle: Keep the herd below 99. Don't be the one who nods off.

howToStepsRaw: On your turn, play one card to change the Herd
Number cards add sheep - but if your play would push the count past 99

Pillows stall or shrink the count (Doze, Counting Backwards, Lullaby, Swap Dreams). Alarms shake it up — Skip a Few, the Black Sheep (snaps to 99), Wide Awake, Heavy Eyelids and Rude Awakening. The Big Bad Wolf hides in the Flock — draw one and a card slot locks for the Night. Not sure what a card does? Press and hold it in your hand, or check The Cards tab above.
Bust the count, or run out of safe cards, and you doze off - you're out for the night. Everyone else plays on from exactly where the Herd sits.

games.pitch: Send the signal. Secure the code.
howToStepsRaw: Your team gets 4 secret keywords numbered 1–4. Only your team can see them — memorise them!
Each round, your Encoder receives a secret code (e.g. 3-1-4). Give one clue per number — cryptic enough to fool the enemy, clear enough for your own team.
The enemy team tries to crack your code first — that's an 🕵️
. Then your own team decodes it. Get it wrong and it's a
🕵️ Intercept — enemy cracked your code. They score.
💥 Misfire — your own team got it wrong. Two misfires and you lose.
First team to reach the interception target wins.
After the main game ends, both teams take turns guessing the other team's vault keywords in order. A second chance to steal the win.

games.pitch: Finally, someone said it.

howToTitle.heading: How to Play 💡
howToTitle.subtitle: Fill in the blank. Vote for the take you relate to most.

howToStepsRaw: Everyone reads The Situation together. It has a blank — that's The Gap you'll fill with your answer.
Pass the phone around. Each player secretly picks a Number and writes something for The Gap. Your combined answer should slot right into the sentence.
All Takes appear at once 🃏, sorted lowest to highest. No names — just the answers. Read them out.
Vote for the take you relate to most. You can't vote for your own.
1st most votes = 3 pts, 2nd = 2 pts, 3rd = 1 pt. Most points across all Situations wins. The take everyone vibes with wins the round.
A mystery Ghost Card joins The Lineup each round. If the group gives The Nod to the Ghost instead of a real player, everyone loses points.
